why: The number of tests the suite must not drop below.
A suite can shrink without any gate noticing. A file whose import breaks
still reports its neighbours as green; a describe block deleted in a merge
resolution leaves no trace; a refactor can lose cases silently. The other
gates all answer 'did what ran pass' — none answers 'did everything still
run'. This is a ratchet, not a target: it fails on a DECREASE only.

Bumped to 487 with kernel-entities-law, to 574 with gate-coverage-strict-path, and again with module-deadlines-civil-date and module-deadlines-thresholds — the two halves of one split, which landed separately and each added 53. Left at its creation value of 317 while the suite grew to 487, the ratchet would have admitted the deletion of every kernel test — review caught that. Bump it in the PR that adds the tests, not later.
Bump this number when a task legitimately adds tests. A task that
legitimately REMOVES them — consolidating cases into one it.each, deleting
a module and its suite — records test_count_waiver on its backlog node with
a reason, exactly as size_total does.
coverage_bp — total repository line coverage, which must not decrease.
In basis points, hundredths of a percent: 7920 means 79.20%. An integer, so
the gate compares integers and never flaps between 79.2 and 79.20, and so
no rounding rule has to be agreed between whoever writes this file and
whoever reads it. Computed from the DA: records in coverage/lcov.info as
covered * 10000 / total, truncated.
The second of two coverage checks, and the one that is not about your task.
gate.sh measures the lines a task CHANGED against 90 (money, compliance,
unknown risk) or 70 (low) — see ADR-030, the floor was never the defect. But
diff coverage alone lets the total rot one uncovered file at a time, every
task green on its own lines, so this ratchets the whole repository: it fails
on a DECREASE only and never on standing still.
Set to 7920 by gate-coverage-strict-path, then raised by module-deadlines-civil-date and module-deadlines-thresholds in turn. 7920 was what the repository
measured at the time (240 of 303 lines). The number is low because six
lib/kernel/*/repository.ts files are Prisma plumbing no unit test can reach.
They are deliberately NOT excluded from coverage — raising them is
kernel-repository-integration-tests, and that node bumps this key.
THIS INTEGER IS ITSELF PART OF THE RATCHET. The gate resolves it from the
PR base as well as from the working tree, because a ratchet read only from
the tree grades itself: edit the number down and the percentage no longer
has to clear anything, the waiver below never runs, and the decrease is
reported as a pass. A value lower here than on the base is treated exactly
as an actual decrease — same waiver, same reason. Raising it is free.
Bump it in the PR that raises coverage, not later; the gate prints the new
value when it sees one. A task that legitimately LOWERS coverage records
coverage_waiver on its backlog node with a coverage_waiver_reason, in basis
points, exactly as test_count_waiver and size_total do.
